analysis_summary: Reviewed the Phase 1 anomalies plus the highest-value AJAX and REST mutation surfaces in BackWPup 5.6.7. No unauthenticated or subscriber/customer-reachable issue was confirmed. Two broken-authorization findings were confirmed for the shipped read-only plugin role `backwpup_check`; major Phase 1 backup-download, logfile-read, and arbitrary-option-update signals were refuted by downstream capability, nonce, and path validation.

reasoning.hypothesis: A user assigned the shipped read-only `backwpup_check` role can reconfigure backup storage and trigger a backup upload to attacker-controlled cloud storage because multiple REST write routes only require the broad `backwpup` capability instead of the narrower edit/start capabilities used elsewhere in the plugin.
trace: `backwpup_check` is created with `backwpup=true`, `backwpup_jobs=true`, and `backwpup_backups=true`, but `backwpup_jobs_edit=false`, `backwpup_jobs_start=false`, and `backwpup_settings=false` in `inc/class-install.php:142-158`.

The read-only role can still access BackWPup admin pages because the Jobs page requires `backwpup_jobs` and the Backups page requires `backwpup_backups` in `inc/class-admin.php:542-547` and `inc/class-admin.php:684-689`.

Any BackWPup admin page receives the REST nonce and write-route URLs because `enqueue_admin_assets()` localizes `backwpupApi` for every screen whose ID contains `backwpup` in `inc/class-admin.php:100-129`, and `get_backwpup_api_data()` exposes `cloudsaveandtest`, `updatejob`, `storages`, and `startbackup` plus `wp_rest` nonce in `inc/class-admin.php:1225-1253`.

The storage write route `/cloudsaveandtest` is registered with `permission_callback => [ $this, 'has_permission' ]` in `src/StorageProviders/API/Rest.php:112-119`, and `has_permission()` only checks `current_user_can('backwpup')` in `src/StorageProviders/API/Rest.php:138-139`.

On a successful call, `cloud_save_and_test()` invokes `$cloud->edit_form_post_save( $jobs )` in `src/StorageProviders/API/Rest.php:262-304`. For S3, `BackWPup_Destination_S3::edit_form_post_save()` persists attacker-controlled `s3accesskey`, `s3secretkey`, `s3bucket`, and `s3dir` into the job record stored under `backwpup_jobs` in `inc/class-destination-s3.php:161-243`.

The same low-privileged actor can then enable that destination because `/updatejob` and `/storages` also use `current_user_can('backwpup')` only, in `src/Jobs/API/Rest.php:87-88`, `src/Jobs/API/Rest.php:97-103`, `src/Jobs/API/Rest.php:381-418`, and `src/StorageProviders/API/Rest.php:122-129`, `src/StorageProviders/API/Rest.php:316-355`.

The same actor can trigger execution with `/startbackup`, which again only uses `current_user_can('backwpup')` in `src/Backups/API/Rest.php:81-82` and `src/Backups/API/Rest.php:94-100`. `start_backup()` calls `$this->job_adapter->get_jobrun_url( 'runnow', $jobid )` in `src/Backups/API/Rest.php:157-260`, which reaches `wp_remote_post()` to `wp-cron.php` in `inc/class-job.php:1850-1887`.

When the job runs with the attacker-controlled S3 settings, `BackWPup_Destination_S3::job_run_archive()` uploads the produced archive via `putObject()` or multipart `uploadPart()` in `inc/class-destination-s3.php:511-551` and `inc/class-destination-s3.php:608-643`, and logs the resulting object URL in `inc/class-destination-s3.php:679-685`.
defenses: The legacy UI consistently treats edit/run actions as privileged: Jobs UI only renders edit/delete for `backwpup_jobs_edit` and run-now for `backwpup_jobs_start` in `inc/class-page-jobs.php:298-304`.
The issue is therefore not intended behavior for the read-only role; the REST layer is weaker than the rest of the plugin's authorization model.

refutation.attempt: Check whether the shipped `backwpup_check` role already includes the narrower edit/start/settings capabilities, which would make the route checks consistent.
Check whether a read-only role can realistically obtain the REST nonce and route URLs needed to invoke these endpoints.
refutation.details: The role can open BackWPup jobs/backups pages, and `enqueue_admin_assets()` plus `get_backwpup_api_data()` expose `wp_rest` nonce and the relevant write endpoints on any BackWPup screen in `inc/class-admin.php:100-129` and `inc/class-admin.php:1225-1253`.

refutation.attempt: Check whether the storage save path is only reachable through a request shape that would not populate `$_POST`, which the destination save methods rely on.
refutation.details: The plugin's own client code sends form-encoded POST data to `cloudsaveandtest` through jQuery AJAX in `assets/js/backwpup-admin.js:826-839` and `assets/js/backwpup-admin.js:1317-1329`, matching the `$_POST` reads in `inc/class-destination-s3.php:163-243`.

reasoning.conclusion: This is a confirmed privilege escalation inside the plugin's own role model. A user who should only inspect jobs/backups can store attacker-controlled cloud credentials, bind them to a job, and trigger a backup upload to attacker-controlled storage, disclosing the site's backup contents.

findings.poc_description: Assign a test account the shipped `backwpup_check` role. Log in and open any BackWPup page to obtain `backwpupApi.nonce`. Use that nonce to POST attacker-controlled S3 parameters to `/wp-json/backwpup/v1/cloudsaveandtest`, then enable S3 for an existing job via `/wp-json/backwpup/v1/updatejob` or `/wp-json/backwpup/v2/storages`, and finally POST `/wp-json/backwpup/v1/startbackup` for that job. The generated archive is uploaded to the attacker-controlled S3 bucket.
findings.remediation: Do not gate write routes with the broad `backwpup` capability. Require route-specific capabilities: storage configuration and destination changes should require `backwpup_jobs_edit` and/or `backwpup_settings`, while backup execution should require `backwpup_jobs_start`. Mirror those checks inside the mutation methods so UI-only gating cannot be bypassed through REST.

reasoning.hypothesis: A `backwpup_check` user can delete stored backup archives through the REST bulk-action endpoint even though the role intentionally lacks `backwpup_backups_delete`.
trace: The REST bulk-delete route `/process_bulk_actions` is exposed with `permission_callback => [ $this, 'has_permission' ]` in `src/Backups/API/Rest.php:122-128`, and `has_permission()` only checks `current_user_can('backwpup')` in `src/Backups/API/Rest.php:81-82`.
`process_bulk_actions()` calls `delete_backup()` for each supplied item in `src/Backups/API/Rest.php:360-385`.
`delete_backup()` resolves the destination from the attacker-supplied `data-url` payload and dispatches to `$dest_class->file_delete( $jobdest, $file )` in `src/Backups/API/Rest.php:395-410`.

For the default local-folder destination, `BackWPup_Destination_Folder::file_delete()` resolves the selected archive under the configured backup directory and deletes it with `wp_delete_file()` in `inc/class-destination-folder.php:62-75`.
defenses: The legacy Backups UI uses the stricter capability consistently: delete buttons are only rendered for `backwpup_backups_delete` in `inc/class-page-backups.php:390-391`, and the legacy delete action dies if that capability is missing in `inc/class-page-backups.php:503-540`.

refutation.attempt: Check whether the role mismatch is only cosmetic in the UI and the backend ultimately enforces `backwpup_backups_delete`.
refutation.details: The REST backend never checks `backwpup_backups_delete`; it only requires `backwpup` before calling `file_delete()`.

refutation.attempt: Check whether the sink is actually an arbitrary-file-delete primitive rather than a backup-only delete path.
refutation.details: `inc/class-destination-folder.php:69-75` constrains deletion to `basename()` under the configured backup directory and requires a real file. The confirmed issue is authorization bypass for backup deletion, not path traversal.

reasoning.conclusion: This is a confirmed authorization bypass for destructive backup actions. The shipped read-only role can delete existing backup archives through REST even though both the role definition and the legacy controller treat backup deletion as a separate privileged action.

findings.poc_description: Assign `backwpup_check` to a test user, log in, load a BackWPup page to obtain `backwpupApi.nonce`, then POST to `/wp-json/backwpup/v1/process_bulk_actions` with `action=delete` and a `backups[0][dataset][data-url]` value copied from a backup row. The selected local backup archive is deleted although the role lacks `backwpup_backups_delete`.
findings.remediation: Require `backwpup_backups_delete` for destructive backup routes, both in the REST route registration and inside the delete handler. Do not reuse the general `backwpup` capability for state-changing operations.

negative_findings.title: AJAX backup download looked unauthenticated at the entry point
negative_findings.reason: The outer AJAX handler in `inc/class-destination-downloader.php:58-99` only parses query arguments, but control immediately reaches `BackWPup_Destinations::file_download()`, which wraps the download in `BackWpup_Download_Handler::verify_request()`. That verifier enforces `check_admin_referer( 'backwpup_action_nonce' )` and `current_user_can( 'backwpup_backups_download' )` before the file is served.

negative_findings.title: AJAX job-progress logfile read as LFI
negative_findings.reason: The candidate at `inc/class-page-jobs.php:1076-1267` is protected by a capability gate plus nonce, and the `logfile` parameter is reduced to `basename()` and must match a `backwpup_log_*.ext` pattern before path construction. That refutes arbitrary-file read and leaves only intended logfile access.

negative_findings.title: AJAX log viewer as arbitrary log/file read
negative_findings.reason: The log viewer requires `backwpup_logs`, verifies a per-log nonce, sanitizes the requested name with `sanitize_file_name()`, and only accepts names containing `backwpup_log_` before resolving the file beneath the configured log directory. No bypass to arbitrary files was confirmed.

negative_findings.title: REST save_site_option as low-priv arbitrary option update
negative_findings.reason: Unlike the broader Jobs REST routes, `/save_site_option` already uses a narrower permission callback: `current_user_can( 'backwpup_jobs_edit' ) || current_user_can( 'backwpup_settings' )` in `src/Jobs/API/Rest.php:331-339`. The handler also blocks critical keys including `backwpup_jobs`, `backwpup_version`, `backwpup_previous_version`, and `backwpup_messages` in `src/Jobs/API/Rest.php:797-814`.

out_of_scope.reason: Exploit requires the shipped custom role `backwpup_check`, not an unauthenticated, subscriber, or customer-equivalent actor.
